name: Luon um la nhau
summary: Lươn um lá nhàu is freshwater eel braised with nhàu leaves and coconut. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam calls it the eel plate to order in U Minh Hạ.
origin: U Minh Hạ. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says eel of 1–2 kg, as thick as a wrist, with yellow skin, is still found in the forest.
taste: Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says the eel is sweet, the coconut milk is rich, and nhàu leaves are sweet-bitter.
howToEat: Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam cleans the slime with wood ash, guts the eel, and marinates it with scallion, garlic, and salt. Nhàu leaves are neither old nor young, with the midrib cut out.
Lemongrass goes on the bottom of the pot, then nhàu, then the eel, then more nhàu. Thin coconut water braises it. Coconut cream goes in at the end.
The dip Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam prints is coconut cream, crushed roasted peanuts, a little tương hột, chili, and fish sauce.

Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam also names cháo lươn bẹ môn, sour eel soup, eel kho with mắm, and eel stir-fried with lemongrass and chili. The braise is the one it singles out. A price was not printed. Check on arrival.
where: U Minh Hạ. No restaurant is named. Check on arrival.
